title: One sky, many views
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Objects emit, absorb and scatter different wavelengths in different ways. Comparing observations across the spectrum can reveal structures and processes a single band misses.

misconception: A learner may choose: Every wavelength always shows identical details
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: Why do astronomers observe the same object at several wavelengths?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: Why do astronomers observe the same object at several wavelengths? Different wavelengths can reveal different physical features. Objects emit, absorb and scatter different wavelengths in different ways. Comparing observations across the spectrum can reveal structures and processes a single band misses.
Visual caption: One object, many wavelengths. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.

recall.question: Why do astronomers observe the same object at several wavelengths?
options: Different wavelengths can reveal different physical features
Every wavelength always shows identical details
A single wavelength measures every property
